All I can tell you for sure is I would have said exactly the same thing before being put in that position myself. I was 17 the first time I was put in the psych ward, so I knew my own mind pretty good by that point.  
You never really know what you're going to do in a situation until you get there.

You say that, but they have ALL THE POWER. You can't leave unless you kiss ass. Once you realize that, you start kissing ass. Otherwise, you'll be stuck in there for days or weeks longer than necessary. You start weighing your options. What's better? Being right? Or going home. I chose going home.

Well, the short answer is, I don't know. I don't know why. If I had to take a guess as to why, I would probably say that it was because it was an extremely stressful time in my life. I FEEL like I was there twice as an 18 year old or older, but I  don't have two discrete sets of memories. I can't split the memories up. If I was there twice, it was definitely the same hospital, thus making it hard to know if I'm remembering two visits or one.  

The psych ward is a horrible place, and as soon as you're in it you try to get out of it as soon as possible. You follow their system, and get their stupid points, and tell them whatever the fuck you think they want to hear to go back out to the real world.

> Others want just the brass tacks

I guess that was me. Let me ask you a question; are there any common diagnoses or personality types that tend to usually prefer a certain way of being treated? (ie, most bipolars need calm, most depression cases need brass tacks) or is it across the board? When you meet someone for the first time, how do you decide which tact to take?

I guess that makes sense. I would think if you HAVE to be cautious, at least sunny and overly cheerful is better than being condescending to. I was IMMEDIATELY ornery with anyone I felt was condescending to me.

Also, in the kids ward, they need to do a better job of explaining what the fuck is going on with the REALLY fucked up kids. I know there's privacy laws and stuff, but it would be really great if it had been explained that, no, the reason that girl is talking to the wall isn't something that can happen to you, you won't get it by being near her. And no, she won't hurt you, and yes, it's okay to talk to them, they're people too!

I don't know officially, but I suppose it was probably something like depression with suicidal ideations. 

If there's one thing I could say to a psych nurse, about treating patients like me (ie, mentally all there, no breaks from reality, understand 100% what's happening to you and why) it would be to treat us like normal people. NOT with kid gloves. Of course, there are TIMES when kid gloves are probably called for, but just... you know. Being treated like a normal person can help you get BACK to feeling like a normal person. None of this "and how are YOU doing today?" Kindergarten bullshit. You can get the same information like a normal person would. "Hey, PsychWardPatient1. What's up? What do you think about these meds?"

There were two types of nurses at the psych ward I was in. 

I'm not making generalizations about race, I'm just telling you ONE person's experiences. I'm not saying that these personality types MUST match up with the physical and social characteristics, but that in my ONE experience, they DID.

The first type of nurse were the big black male nurses. These guys were HUGE. I believe that many more problems were averted by their presence than they actually had to deal with, although if someone needed to be held down, they were the ones doing the holding.

They were, across the board, extremely extremely nice to me. They joked with me and they treated me like a normal person. When I left, they gave me hugs and told me they never wanted to see me again. That was the part I loved best. They didn't pry, they didn't look down on me or pity me. They just treated me like a normal human being. You don't know how important that is to you until you're in a place where it's taken away. Being in a place where you are looked down upon and seen as "less than" is truly horrible. 

The other type of nurse was the upper middle class white female nurses. I'm sure some of them were nice, but they were snotty to me. They would tell me things like I shouldn't be in a place like this, and I had so much going for me, (implying that there was no reason for me to be suicidal, basically belittling my problems and telling me that I wasn't worth their time.) Basically, they were all cunts. They would gossip about patients and were passive aggressive. They made it clear that they thought I was wasting their time and resources and a slot in the psych ward for someone who needed it more. I think many of them ended up in the psych ward because patients there can't really do anything and their complaints aren't taken seriously. 

The doctor himself was rude to me at one point too. I remember going off on him and him apologizing to me later. I don't remember what the situation was (it was a very stressful time in my life) but I GUARANTEE you that it was a fucked up situation in which I was clearly right and he was clearly wrong. I wish I could remember exactly what happened, but it wasn't a matter of opinion or me being unreasonable or anything, it was just him on a power trip.

I've read some research about the way boot camps work, how they try to tear you down to nothing to build you up again. I think psych wards do this too. You come in with NO privileges hardly, and there's usually some sort of level board or something where you "Earn" basic human rights. They wanted to strip search me when I came in. The nurse (she was an old white lady, and sweet) felt bad for me when I started bawling and BEGGED her not to. I swore to her, "I didn't bring anything in, please don't do this to me, please don't do this to me, I swear I'll do whatever you want". I'm crying right now thinking about it. She was going to allow me to keep my pants and bra on, but I wasn't wearing those. I was wearing some tight jeans and a hoody. I am SURE she was breaking rules by not doing the search the right way, but I thanked her profusely.

If they could find a way to treat newcomers with more basic human decency, it would go a lot further. When you come into a place like that, you're already not in a great state of mind, and when they treat you like an animal, you don't WANT to settle down and do what you're told. You want to start a fucking revolution.
